name: Locksmith
what: A PowerShell tool that finds common Active Directory Certificate Services misconfigurations (the ESC-class issues used in the community taxonomy) and can propose or apply fixes. It is the defensive complement to an authorised Certipy run: read-only modes write findings to the console or CSV, and a separate remediation mode offers to fix issues after warning about possible operational impact.
when: At the start of an AD CS hardening programme, and again after you change templates, CA flags or enrollment endpoints. Use it on a domain-joined management host against forests you own or have written permission to assess.
cost_note: The Gallery module is free. The licence is MIT plus Commons Clause: you may not sell a product or service whose value derives substantially from Locksmith.
example: On a domain-joined host that already has the ActiveDirectory and ServerManager PowerShell modules, install from the PowerShell Gallery: `Install-Module -Name Locksmith -Scope CurrentUser` (Gallery release 2026.11.62109 was current when this page was checked on 8 November 2026).
Run a read-only forest scan that prints findings as a table (Mode 0, the default): `Invoke-Locksmith`.

For evidence you can attach to a change record, write issues to CSV with `Invoke-Locksmith -Mode 2` (creates ADCSIssues.CSV in the current directory) or issues plus example fixes with `Invoke-Locksmith -Mode 3` (ADCSRemediation.CSV).

Narrow the run with `-Scans` when you are chasing a specific class, for example `Invoke-Locksmith -Scans ESC1,ESC8`. Documented scan names include All, Auditing, ESC1 through ESC9, ESC11, ESC13, ESC15, ESC16, EKEUwu and PromptMe.
Map each row to the AD CS hardening guide and apply fixes through change control. Do not use Mode 4 (fix all issues) in production.
pitfalls: Mode 4 identifies misconfigurations and offers to fix each one. The author describes it as an easy button and says Locksmith will warn when a fix may have operational impact — still treat it as a production change, not a scan.
Some checks and all remediation need administrative rights. A standard-user run under-reports CA-level issues such as ESC6 and ESC7.
The host must be domain-joined and the ActiveDirectory and ServerManager modules must be present before you import Locksmith.
Older bookmarks pointing at github.com/TrimarcJake/Locksmith redirect to jakehildreth/Locksmith; use the current repository and the PowerShell Gallery module name Locksmith.
Run it only against environments you own or have written permission to test.
